nodes.name: BP nanoflakes exfoliation
nodes.procedure: 20 mg bulk BP was added into 20 mL saturated NaOH/NMP. The dispersion was sonicated for 4 h by using a tip sonicator (Misonix XL-2000) under ice cooling at 10 W output power. After that, the dispersion was centrifuged at 2000 rpm for 20 minutes two times to remove nonexfoliated bulk BP, resulting in BP nanoflakes NMP dispersions (0.2 mg mL⁻¹).

nodes.name: CN nanosheets synthesis
nodes.procedure: 10 g urea powders were dissolved into 15 mL water under stirring condition. The pH of solution was adjusted to 4~5 by using HCl (0.1 M). The solution was dried at 60 °C for 12 h and then transfer to a crucible with a lid. After that, the crucible was heated to 550 °C in muffle furnace at a heating rate of 10 °C min⁻¹. The precursor was maintained at 550 °C for 2 h and cool down to room temperature naturally, resulting in CN nanosheets.

nodes.name: BP/CN nanohybrid formation
nodes.procedure: 12 mg CN into 10 mL NMP solvent and then with ultrasonication to form a homogeneous dispersion. Afterwards, the 15 mL as-prepared BP NMP dispersion was added into CN dispersion with sonication for 2 h. The mixtures were kept stirring overnight. The powders were collected by high-speed centrifugation and washed with ethanol thoroughly, and then dried in an oven at 40 °C overnight, resulting in BP/CN. The weight ratio of BP:CN was 1:4.

nodes.characterization_summary: BP shows thin sheet-like structure 100 nm–1 μm. CN shows silk-like structure 100–800 nm. BP nanoflakes attached on CN nanosheets surface.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Transmission electron microscopy (TEM) image of BP shows thin sheet-like structure with the size of 100 nm ∼ 1 μm (Fig. 1a)... Figure 1e clearly shows that BP nanoflakes were attached on the surface of CN nanosheets.

nodes.characterization_summary: BP shows lattice fringes d=0.26 nm (040) plane. CN shows amorphous structure.
nodes.evidence_snippet: From high resolution TEM (HRTEM), clear lattice fringes with d-spacing of 0.26 nm corresponds to the (040) plane were observed from BP layers (Fig. 1b)... the HRTEM image indicates amorphous structures (Fig. 1d).

nodes.characterization_summary: BP diffraction peaks consistent with JCPDS No. 73-1358 with changed intensities due to oriented {010} facets. CN shows peaks at 13.0° (100) and 27.3° (002). BP/CN shows both BP and CN peaks with (040)/(111) ratio of 0.4/1.
nodes.evidence_snippet: XRD patterns (Fig. 1f) show that all diffraction peaks of BP are consistent well with the standard pattern (JCPDS No. 73-1358)... For BP/CN, both typical diffraction peaks of BP and CN were observed.

nodes.characterization_summary: HAADF-STEM and EDX elemental mapping show uniform hybridization of BP and CN with green (N, CN) and red (P, BP) areas.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The HAADF-STEM image of these pieces of BP/CN hybrids and corresponding EDX elemental mapping of P and N elements evidently indicate the uniform hybridization of BP and CN (Fig. 2).

XPS spectra were measured to clearly show C 1s and N 1s in CN and BP/CN, and P 2p in BP and BP/CN (Figs. S7 and 3)... The higher and lower binding energy shifts of N 1s and P 2p in BP/CN are ascribed to the decrease and increase of the electron density of CN and BP, respectively.

nodes.characterization_summary: BP/CN shows new peak ~960 cm⁻¹ assigned to P-N stretching confirming coordinate bond formation.
nodes.evidence_snippet: a small new peak located at around 960 cm⁻¹ was observed. This peak is assigned to P−N stretching mode, confirming the generation P-N coordinate bond in the BP/CN composites.

nodes.characterization_summary: BP: 17.5 ppm (P-P). BP/CN: 17.1 ppm (free BP), -0.2 ppm, 5.4 ppm (P-N bonds).
nodes.evidence_snippet: Fig. S11 shows the ³¹P NMR of pure BP with a peak around 17.5 ppm... For BP/CN, a peak around 17.1 ppm was observed to be assigned to free BP. Beside this peak, two additional peaks around -0.2 and 5.4 ppm were observed, which are assigned to P-N coordinate bonds.

nodes.characterization_summary: BP: broad UV-NIR absorption edge ~1740 nm. CN: absorption edge 463 nm (Eg=2.7 eV). BP/CN: CN edge red-shifted to 470 nm + BP tail.
nodes.evidence_snippet: BP nanoflakes exhibit a very broad absorption in UV to NIR region with an absorption edge around 1740 nm. In contrast, CN nanosheets display a visible absorption edge around 463 nm, indicating a bandgap of 2.7 eV.

nodes.characterization_summary: AFM shows fine morphology of BP and CN.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Atomic force microscopy (AFM) shows the fine morphology of as-prepared BP and CN (Figs. S1 and S2).

nodes.characterization_summary: SAED shows high quality crystalline state of exfoliated BP nanoflakes.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The selected-area electron diffraction (SAED) and Raman spectra (Fig. S4) show high quality of crystalline state for exfoliated BP nanoflakes.

nodes.characterization_summary: EDX analysis of components of BP, CN, and BP/CN. EDX elemental mapping shows uniform P/N distribution in BP/CN.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The components of BP, CN, and BP/CN were also analyzed by EDX (Fig. S5)... corresponding EDX elemental mapping of P and N elements evidently indicate the uniform hybridization of BP and CN (Fig. 2).

nodes.characterization_summary: 13C NMR of BP/CN shows little chemical shift vs pure CN, no new peaks, indicating weak C-P interaction.
nodes.evidence_snippet: the ¹³C NMR of pure CN and BP/CN nanocomposites were studied (Fig. S12). Compare to pure CN, the chemical shifts of the BP/CN show little shift... This result suggests that C elements do not have strong interaction with P in the BP/CN composites.

nodes.characterization_summary: Raman spectra confirm high quality crystalline state of exfoliated BP nanoflakes.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The selected-area electron diffraction (SAED) and Raman spectra (Fig. S4) show high quality of crystalline state for exfoliated BP nanoflakes.
